sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the disputes between the petitioner and respondent No.2 arose out of the marriage and matrimonial relation between petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2.

The matter having been referred to Mediation, the disputes between the parties have been resolved by way of Mediation and settlement agreement has been arrived at under Section 89 of the CPC read with Rule 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules,
2005 and in furtherance thereof that he submits that parties have agreed for the criminal proceedings to be quashed by allowing the present petition.
3. All the parties are present before this Court and they are identified by their respective counsel.
On enquiry all of them submit that the settlement which has been arrived at before the Meditation Centre is voluntarily without any force or coercsion.

A joint NC: 2024:KHC:14669 memo has been filed singed by petitioners their counsel, respondent No.2 and their counsel, which reads as under:
JOINT MEMO BY PETITIONERS AND RESPONDENT No.2

The Petitioners and Respondent No.2 abovenamed most humbly beg to submit jointly as under:
1.
The Petitioners have filed the above Petition to Quash the entire Proceedings in C.C. No.15178 of 2017 pending on the file of the Honourable XLVI Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: 2. The Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the Parents of the Petitioner No.1 and Petitioner No.4 is the daughter of Petitioner No.2 and 3 and Sister of Petitioner No.1.
The Petitioner No.1 and Respondent No.2 are the husband and Wife and their marriage was solemnized on 10.05.2015 at C.K. Convention Inn.
At Bengaluru.
Rajarajeshwari Nagar,

3. Owing to the differences of opinion between the Respondent No.2 and the Petitioner No.1 the Respondent No.2 filed a Petition under Section 9 of The Hindu Marriage Act, in M.C No.550 of 2016 and the Petitioner No.1 filed a Petition under Section 13 (1) (a) and (b) of The Hindu Marriage Act,
to dissolve their marriage in M.C. No.6368 of 17, and both the Petitions were clubbed together and pending on the file of the Honourable IV Addl Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru.

5.

In terms of the Settlement, the Petitioner No.1 paid a sum of 3,00,000/- by Demand Draft bearing No. 001634 Dated 18.1.2024 drawn on HDFC Bank, Ideal Homes Township Branch, R.R.
Nagar, Bengaluru in favour of Respondent No.2, and paid the same and on receipt of the same, the Respondent No.2 withdrew the Petition in M.C. No.550 of 2016 and Decreed the Petition in M.C.
No.6368 of 2017 and dissolved the marriage between the Petitioner No.1 and Respondent No.2, and further the Petitioner No.1 paid a sum of 2,00,000/- by Demand Draft bearing No.001637 Dated 20.1.2024 drawn on HDFC Bank, Ideal Homes Township Branch, R.R. Nagar, Bengaluru and on receipt of the same, the Respondent No.2 withdrew the Petition in C. Mis. No.32 of 2017.

The Copy of the Decree Passed in M.C.No.6368 of 2017 is herewith produce for kind perusal of this Honorable Court as Document No.2.
6.

Nagar, Bengaluru on this day, Before this Honorable Court in the above case, and the Respondent No.2 hereby acknowledges the receipt of the said amount, and the entire Amount of Rs.8,00,000/- from the Petitioner No.1 towards Permanent Alimony in full and final settlement of all her claims.

The Copy of the Demand Draft bearing No.857486 Dated 30.1.2024 is herewith NC:
2024:KHC:14669 produce for kind perusal of this Honorable Court as Document No.3.
7.

In view of the above, the Respondent No.2 does not intend to prosecute the case in C.C. No.15178 of 2017 pending on the file of the Honourable XLVI Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru,

sentences.text: In terms of said joint memo the parties have reiterated the settlement arrived at before the Mediation Center for sum of Rs.8,00,000/- as permanent alimony in full and final settlement of all the claims to respondent No.2 against the petitioner.

Out of the said amount an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- is stated to have been paid by way of demand draft bearing No.001634 dated 18.1.2024 drawn on HDFC Bank, Ideal Homes Township Branch, R.R.Nagar, Bengaluru.
A further sum of Rs.2,00,000/- was paid by demand draft bearing No.001637 dated 20.1.2024 drawn on HDFC Bank, Ideal Homes Township Branch, R.R.Nagar, Bengaluru.

Today another demand draft for a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- drawn in favour of respondent No.2 bearing No.857486 dated 30.1.2024 drawn on HDFC Bank, Ideal Homes Township Branch, R.R.Nagar, Bengaluru has been handed over to the respondent No.2.
5. Smt.Sandhya Rani.
K.S-respondent No.2 who is present before this Court in person
confirms receipt of the aforesaid amount of Rs.3,00,000/- and Rs.2,00,000/- as indicated above and the demand draft for sum of Rs.3,00,000/- handed over today.

She confirms that the receipt of the aforesaid NC: 2024:KHC:14669 amounts is in full and final settlement of all her claims against petitioner No.1-husband and his family member who are arrayed as petitioners No.2 to 4 to the present petition.

The Petitioners confirm that they have no claim against Respondent no.2.
6.

The present proceedings arising out of matrimonial relationship and the offences alleged being that under Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Provision Act, 1961, Section 498 A, 506 read with Section 34 of the IPC, I am of the considered opinion that the settlement arrived at between the parties has put to an end all the matrimonial disputes between the parties.
The proceedings in Crime No.204/2016 now pending as cc no.15178/2017 would also have been quashed.

In that view of the matter, I pass the following;
ORDER i.
The Criminal petition is allowed.
The proceedings in Crime No.204/2016 registered by the Rajarajeshwari Nagar Police Station is now pending in CC No.15178/2017 pending on the file on the III Add.
Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore has now transferred to the 46th Add.
Chief Metropolitan Magistrates, Bangalore are hereby quashed.

Sd/-
